about: What a host must do when a checking provider breaks a rule that no schema can express. `run` says how the one run ended. `outcome` is `verdict` with the verdict the host records, or `refused` with the reason. Nothing may be recorded as passed except in the control and in the cases whose outcome is the verdict `passed`. `ran` false means no run may have started; `runs` is how many must have.

cases.why: A control: a provider that keeps every rule must be accepted, or the other cases prove nothing.
A run that did not exit ends the check in error. The provider is not asked what it thinks.
An executor that cannot be reached is reported as exactly that.
A verdict rests on a run.
A result may not claim more than the manifest declares.
A verdict that states no strength claims one the host cannot bound.
The set of verdicts is closed.
An answer asks for a run or gives a verdict, never both.
An answer that does neither is no answer.
A provider may start only tools it declared.
The same holds for a tool named in an argument.
A program path lies inside the tool it names.
So does a file of a tool named in an argument.
A run starts inside its working directory.
A run writes inside its working directory.
A run may read only what its result is keyed by.
A later run may use only what is in the key.
An answer matches its request.
What a provider says a file contains is never taken on its word.
The same holds for a file it attaches to its verdict: the bytes are hashed again.
An attachment lies inside the working directory.
A check may ask for the same run twice, to see whether a result repeats. Each is submitted under its own key, which includes its number, so the second is never answered from the first.
A tool the manifest declares but the check was not given is not in the key of its result, so a run may not start it.
The same holds for such a tool named in an argument.
A tool named in an argument is a tool named, with or without a file after it.
Every tool named in an argument is looked at, not only the first.
A run uses the tools the check was given, by digest. Another digest is another tool.
The tools a run lists are among those the check was given.
An argument holds no NUL: what follows it would be cut off or read as something else.
A result states the class of strength the manifest declares. A test is not a proof, whatever its rank.
A failure rests on a run as much as a pass does.
The ceiling holds for a failure as for a pass.
An answer carries the id of its request.
The opening echo must come back unchanged, or the two sides do not read text the same way.
A check may ask for eight runs. The ninth is refused before it starts.
A control for the limit: exactly eight runs are allowed.
